oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Study on evolution law of water-conducting fracture zone in steeply inclined coal seam longwall fully-mechanized top-coal caving face
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: To study the development height of the water-conducting fracture zone (WCFZ) in the steeply inclined longwall fully-mechanized top-coal caving face, the 202 fully-mechanized caving face in the west No.2 mining area of Wangjiashan Coal Mine was taken as the research object, and comprehensive methods including empirical formula calculation, physical similarity simulation, numerical simulation and on-site actual measurement were adopted to analyze the dynamic evolution law of the water-conducting fractured zone in steeply inclined coal seams. The results show that the filling degree of caved rocks in the goaf presents a distribution characteristic of inclined middle part > inclined lower part > inclined upper part. Due to the existence of an articulated structure in the inclined lower part, a large-scale void space is formed in the goaf; meanwhile, since the height of the water-conducting fracture zone has penetrated the roof aquifer, this area is prone to water accumulation. With the advancement of the working face, the continuous instability of the overlying strata reduces the pressure on the void space, resulting in the formation of confined water in the accumulated water. In the inclined direction of the working face, the water-conducting fracture zone (WCFZ) of the steeply inclined longwall fully-mechanized top-coal caving face presents an asymmetric trapezoidal shape. During initial mining, the highest point of the development height of fracture zone is located in the upper-middle part of the working face along the incline; with the continuous advancement of the working face, this highest point gradually shifts to the upper part of the incline and finally stabilizes there. The evolutionary law of the WCFZ shape obtained by physical simulation is basically consistent with that of numerical simulation. The fracture-mining ratio calculated by empirical formula ranges from 10.6 to 16.2, the value obtained from physical similar material simulation is 10.46, and that from numerical simulation is 16.63. Field measured data indicate that the final vertical height of the water-conducting fracture zone reaches 150.81 m, corresponding to a fracture-mining ratio of 16.67. This result is in good agreement with the upper limit of the empirical formula calculation and the numerical simulation result.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A prediction model and zonal evaluation method for concealed fault density based on VMD-SABO-XGBoost
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Concealed fault is an important geological problem in coal mine production. The scale of concealed fault is often small and it is difficult to predict accurately. In order to study the machine learning optimization algorithm suitable for predicting concealed faults, a prediction model for concealed fault density and a zonal evaluation method of fault complexity based on VMD-SABO-XGBoost are proposed, and the variational mode decomposition (VMD) algorithm is used to decompose the initial data such as gas content and firmness coefficient collected in the mine site into multiple modal components, and the feature extraction is carried out. The grey correlation analysis method is used to calculate the correlation degree ranking of the predicted features. Among them, the five characteristic indexes of fault strength parameters, fault fractal dimension, gas content, coal seam floor dip angle variation coefficient and firmness coefficient have the greatest correlation with fault occurrence. The elite reverse learning and adaptive weight factor are introduced into subtraction-average-based optimizer (SABO) optimization algorithm to solve the problems that the model falls into the “local optimal solution” prematurely, the convergence performance is poor and the diversity of the characteristic population is insufficient. The accuracy difference of the algorithm before and after optimization is verified by experiments. It is proved that the optimized SABO greatly improves the convergence efficiency and the prediction accuracy of the model. Combined with extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) machine learning algorithm, a concealed fault prediction model is formed. Taking the fault of 3# coal heading face in a mine in Changzhi, Shanxi Province as the experimental object, the comprehensive zonal evaluation grade of fault type is established, and it is used as a prediction label to compare with the traditional XGBoost model, VMD-XGBoost model and SABO-XGBoost model. The results show that the VMD-SABO-XGBoost model has the highest prediction accuracy. A prediction model for concealed fault density and a partition evaluation method of fault complexity based on VMD-SABO-XGBoost are proposed. The accuracy and adaptability of the method are verified by an example, which is corresponding to the actual fault complexity in the field. It can be applied to predict the density and complexity of concealed faults in mines.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Study on the influence mechanism of interface dip angle on damage and failure of coal-rock combinations under confining pressure
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: To investigate the failure and instability mechanism of coal-rock combinations with different interface dip angles, a series of conventional triaxial compression simulation tests under a confining pressure of 4 MPa were conducted on coal-rock combinations with dip angles of 0°, 15°, 30°, 45°, and 60° using discrete element numerical simulation software. The mechanical properties, stress evolution, crack evolution, failure patterns, and acoustic emission (AE) signals of the coal-rock combinations were systematically studied, and the failure mechanism was further explored. The results show that with the increase in dip angle, the peak strength and total number of cracks of the coal-rock combinations gradually decrease; the elastic modulus increases significantly only at a dip angle of 60°; the crack propagation direction changes with the increase in dip angle, indicating a variation in the failure mode of the coal-rock combinations. The final failure pattern gradually transforms from an “X” shape to a “V” shape with increasing dip angle, and the failure region gradually approaches the lower right of the coal body and the interface, with cracks also appearing in some parts of the rock mass. At a dip angle of 60°, the failure surface is parallel to the interface. The duration of AE signals decreases and the peak occurs earlier with increasing dip angle, suggesting that the final failure degree of the coal-rock combinations reduces but the failure time advances. With the increase in dip angle, the failure mode of the coal-rock combinations gradually changes from shear failure to interface slip failure, and the failure region shifts from the coal body to the interface. At small dip angles, the interface effect is weak, and the failure of the combinations is mainly controlled by their material properties. With the increase in dip angle, the interface effect becomes significant, and slip dislocation becomes the dominant failure mode. Under large dip angle conditions, the final failure of the coal-rock combinations is mainly attributed to the structural instability of the interface.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Design of a mining rotary visual borehole detector
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In the complex working environment of coal mines, accurately detecting geological conditions such as fissures, separations, and fractured zones inside boreholes is a crucial step in preventing major safety accidents. With the iterative upgrading of intelligent mining technologies, the demand for the precision and timeliness of transparent geological models has increased exponentially, posing unprecedented challenges to borehole detection techniques. There is an urgent need to achieve a realistic representation of geological structures and precise detection of fine structures. Existing various borehole detection instruments have shortcomings: the viewing angle of camera probes is generally limited, making it difficult to fully capture borehole wall information; the video clarity is poor, resulting in the failure to clearly present key details such as micro-fractures; the effect of image unfolding and stitching is unsatisfactory, which affects the integrity and accuracy of geological data. To address these issues, a visual borehole detection solution is proposed, and a mining rotary visual borehole detector is designed. The instrument adopts a novel borehole imaging technology, and the imaging probe can switch freely between forward viewing and side viewing at any angle, enabling clear acquisition of both the front structures and side details inside the borehole; it supports focal length adjustment and brightness adjustment functions to adapt to different detection environments; a unique lens self-cleaning device effectively addresses lens contamination caused by dust and mud in underground mines. In terms of video image processing, the rectangular image unfolding algorithm based on borehole center positioning and the video image stitching algorithm based on feature matching eliminate interference caused by natural jitter and rotation of the camera, significantly improving the unfolding and stitching quality of panoramic borehole images. Verified through ground and underground borehole tests, the mining rotary visual borehole detector has demonstrated excellent performance: it features high video image resolution with clear and complete frames, capable of accurately presenting subtle structures such as millimeter-scale fractures on the borehole wall; the measured data is stable and reliable, and the error control fully meets industry standards; it has a wide range of application scenarios, suitable for various boreholes including water exploration and drainage holes, gas drainage holes, anchor holes, and geological exploration holes, realizing the true reproduction and accurate detection of internal structures for borehole.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Multi-dimensional inhibition effect of halogen salt inhibitors on coal spontaneous combustion in goaf
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Spraying inhibitors in the goaf can prevent and control coal spontaneous combustion. To investigate the effects of different halogen salt inhibitors and their mass fractions on the prevention and control of spontaneous combustion of residual coal in the goaf, the 51102 working face of Jintong Mining Co., Ltd. was taken as the research background (the mined coal seam is Class Ⅰ easy-to-spontaneous-combustion coal seam, and the coal dust is explosive, leading to a high risk of spontaneous combustion). The inhibition performance of inhibitors was analyzed through temperature-programmed experiments coupled with gas chromatography and thermogravimetric tests, and the optimal inhibitor type and spraying concentration were optimized. Furthermore, the inhibition mechanism of inhibitors on coal spontaneous combustion was revealed via molecular dynamics simulation. The results show that the inhibition efficiency of different inhibitors ranks as MgCl2·6H2O > CaCl2·2H2O > NaCl. The difference in inhibition performance is small at low temperatures but gradually increases with rising temperature. The inhibition performance of halogen salt inhibitors is positively correlated with their mass fractions; however, the growth rate of inhibition efficiency gradually decreases with increasing mass fraction. Considering both inhibition effect and economic benefit, MgCl2·6H2O with a mass fraction of 15 %-20 % is determined as the optimal inhibitor. The interaction energies of the three inhibitor systems follow the order of NaCl < CaCl2 < MgCl2, indicating that MgCl2 exhibits the strongest adsorption capacity on the coal surface. For MgCl2 systems with five mass fractions, an inhibition adsorption peak appears at approximately 30 Å (1 Å = 10−10 m). The inhibition adsorption peak is relatively high at a mass fraction of 15%-20%, and the mean square displacement and diffusion coefficient of MgCl2 molecules in the system are small under this condition, demonstrating the strongest adsorption capacity of MgCl2 on the coal surface. Based on the optimization results, a solution with a mass fraction of 15% MgCl2·6H2O solution was applied as the inhibitor for coal spontaneous combustion prevention in the goaf. The measured temperatures at monitoring points in the goaf stably remained below 60 ℃, showing an excellent inhibition effect.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Study on microscopic fractal characteristics and seepage mechanism of tectonically deformed coal with different particle sizes
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: To investigate the regulatory mechanism of particle size on the microstructure and seepage characteristics of tectonically deformed coal, and further provide theoretical support for gas disaster prevention and control as well as high-efficiency coal mining in tectonically deformed coal-bearing areas, this study took the tectonically deformed coal and primary coal from Erdaogou Coal Mine in Aiweiergou Mining Area of Xinjiang as the research objects. Scanning electron microscope (SEM) was employed to observe the micro-pore characteristics of coal samples classified into five particle size ranges: [425, 850) μm, [250, 425) μm, [180, 250) μm, [150, 180) μm and [125, 150) μm. Combined with image binarization processing and box-counting fractal method, the fractal characteristics of the micro-pore structure of tectonically deformed coal with different particle sizes were quantitatively characterized. Based on fractal theory, a coal mass seepage model was established to systematically reveal the intrinsic influence mechanism of particle size effect on the seepage characteristics of tectonically deformed coal. The results indicate that: the pores of primary coal are densely distributed with poor connectivity, while the pore types of tectonically deformed coal are dominated by fragment pores, mineral-filled pores and breccia pores, presenting diverse and complex morphologies. With the decrease in particle size of tectonically deformed coal, the complexity and heterogeneity of its micro-pore characteristics are continuously enhanced. The calculation results of fractal dimension show that the fractal dimension of tectonically deformed coal increases gradually with the reduction of particle size, which directly reflects the improvement of the complexity of micro-pore characteristics. The calculation results of the fractal seepage model reveal that the permeability of tectonically deformed coal is significantly correlated with microstructural parameters such as fractal dimension and pore diameter. Specifically, a larger fractal dimension corresponds to a higher proportion of small pores during the seepage process, which consequently leads to a significant increase in the seepage resistance of coal mass.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Productivity characteristics and main controlling factors of coalbed methane wells in Gujiao Block
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Coalbed methane (CBM) resources are abundant in Gujiao Block at the central part of Xishan Coalfield, where the production capacity of the regional single well varies greatly due to multiple factors, and the large-scale development of CBM faces severe challenges. Aiming at the problems such as insufficient understanding and unclear main control factors of the productivity characteristics of gas well No.8+9 in Gujiao Block, based on the analysis of regional CBM reservoir formation geological background, developing dynamic data and productivity factors, grey correlation analysis was carried out on regional CBM wells from six aspects of burial depth, resource abundance, permeability, sealing condition, coal structure and skin coefficient based on the average daily gas production of a single well, and the correlation degree was sorted. Finally, the main controlling factors of coalbed methane well productivity in Gujiao Block are determined. The research results indicate that the productivity of CBM wells shows strong heterogeneity, with average of daily gas production in range of 80-1 900 m3/d; the high production wells are mainly distributed in Zhongshe slope zone, Nanshan syncline zone and Longzigou slope zone, while the relative poor production wells distributed in nose-shaped structural zone; the main controlling factors for the productivity of CBM wells include sealing condition, resource abundance and coal structure. Sealing conditions affect the preservation of CBM, resource abundance controls the material basis of CBM, and coal structure affects the permeability conditions of coal reservoirs. Finally, a regional CBM enrichment and high-yield model based on high resource abundance, strong sealing condition and complete coal structure is proposed. This model shows that the key to realizing the high yield of coalbed methane production wells in Gujiao Block is to find the productive potential area under rich material foundation, favorable cover layer conditions and good seepage channel.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Characterization of surface contact modes of rough fractures in coal and their influence on seepage
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: To further explore the control mechanism of contact characteristics of rough fracture surfaces in coal on coalbed methane (CBM) migration, enhance the understanding of CBM seepage laws, and better support the efficient exploitation of CBM, this study proposes a 3D rough fracture generation algorithm with controllable surface contact modes by combining the quaternary structure generation set (QSGS) algorithm and the Weierstrass-Mandelbrot function. oai_dc:dc.dc:title: High temperature disrupts nectarine (Prunus persica var. nectarina) pollen development via meiotic impairment, callose dysregulation, tapetal dysfunction and oxidative stress
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: High temperature at microspore mother cell stage is one of most important environmental constraints affecting pollen fertility and nectarine yield. This study investigated the impact of high temperature at the microspore mother cell (MMC) stage on pollen development and antioxidant enzyme characteristics in nectarine (Prunus persica var. nectarina), elucidating mechanisms underlying high temperature-induced pollen abortion to provide scientific insights for mitigating heat stress in protected cultivation. Results demonstrated that high temperature severely disrupted meiosis, significantly reducing normal tetrad formation while increasing triads and polyads. Subsequent microspore development exhibited abnormalities including multinucleated and hollow-deformed structures at the uninucleate and bicellular stages. Furthermore, high temperature caused uneven callose deposition around MMCs, resulting in wall fissures and premature exposure of tetrads due to diminished peripheral callose. Critically, tapetal cells – vital for nutrient supply – initiated premature vacuolation during the MMC stage. Instead of undergoing normal degradation at the uninucleate microspore phase, these cells exhibited progressive vacuolation and expansion, physically constricting microspores and disrupting nutrient provision. Concurrently, high temperature-suppressed antioxidant enzyme activity throughout pollen development while elevating reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, inducing oxidative membrane damage. Collectively, 56.1% pollen abortion under high temperature stress primarily stems from meiotic irregularities, dysregulated callose deposition, delayed tapetal degradation, and ROS-mediated metabolic imbalance. These findings establish critical physiological and cytological foundations for enhancing nectarine thermotolerance in horticultural production systems.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Temporal trends in antimicrobial consumption and an investigation of hospital antimicrobial stewardship activities through structured interviews
oai_dc:dc.dc:description:
Abstract
Objective: Although antimicrobial consumption data are routinely collected, linking these data to the actual antimicrobial stewardship program (ASP) remains challenging. The objective of the present study is to explore association between temporal trends in three categories of antimicrobial consumption and actually implemented of ASPs, in acute care hospitals through structured interviews.
Design: Multicenter retrospective study with structured interviews.
Setting: Japanese hospitals.
Methods: Temporal trends in three antimicrobial consumption data including days of therapy (DOT) per 1,000 patient-days (PD), days of antibiotic spectrum coverage (DASC) per 1,000 PD, and DASC/DOT were collected from 10 hospitals between 2016 and 2024. Structured interviews to identify current ASP progression and challenges related to ASP promotion were conducted.
Results: Ten hospitals participated in the study. Although all participating hospitals had implemented ASPs, most had introduced one or two core ASP interventions. The most commonly implemented ASP was post-prescription review and feedback for broad-spectrum antimicrobials. Despite the presence of ASPs, 50% of hospitals (5/10) demonstrated unfavorable changes in trends across all three metrics, characterized by increasing DASC, DOT, and DASC/DOT. Structured interviews identified various barriers to advancing ASP, including clinical pharmacist shortages, suboptimal infrastructure, limited financial or political support and insufficient knowledge and clinical experience related to ASP activities.
Conclusions: The presence of ASPs in Japan did not consistently lead to changes in antimicrobial prescribing practices, as reflected in antimicrobial consumption metrics. Integrating longitudinal antimicrobial consumption data with structured qualitative assessments provides a more comprehensive understanding of ASP progression and promotion at the institutional level.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Some peculiar landforms over a large area (about 400,000 km ^2 ) of Amazonis Planitia on subequatorial Mars include groups of parallel erosion marks (“grooves”) that are some kilometers long and 2 km wide, bright on darker terrain, and associated with light areas interpreted as open fractures hundreds of kilometers wide (“sliding terrain”), mounds located at one end of the grooves, sinuous folds in the rugged terrain, and kilometer-wide blocks that have been roto-translated from their initial position. Similar features in other Martian areas (in particular Athabasca–Cerberus) have been earlier attributed either to volcanic action or to displacement of ice plates. Here the combined analysis of the landforms with mathematical estimates is consistent with the model of floating ice extending over the northern part of Amazonis Planitia. An initial phase, with ice floating on water (likely an ocean), was followed by a drop in water level. As the ice floes came into contact with the gently sloping floor, they no longer floated on an equipotential surface. Tension increased and ice repeatedly broke into smaller pieces that moved for some kilometers, pushed by the weak gradients. The large, bright areas are the product of such fractures. Grooves were formed by ice sliding on the ground, and collisions between floes produced pressure ridges. The depth of the grooves and of sliding terrain, on the order of a few meters, indicates the thickness of the ice sheet, comparable to that of the present-day Arctic. Dating of the ice sliding events and other features are found to be incompatible with volcanic processes.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: How are shrine forests managed? The increased need for monitoring and awareness for biodiversity conservation in potential OECMs
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Shrine forests, which are forests growing within shrine areas, are one of the potential Other Effective area-based Conservation Measures (OECMs), but their management status is not well surveyed owing to their religious characteristics. A clear governance structure for decision-making by religious corporations as landowners is a key foundation for involving societal collaborators such as local residential supporters (Ujiko), worshippers (Sukeisha) and visitors (Sanpaisha). For shrine forests to be identified, recognized and reported as OECMs, a cooperation system connected with multi-level policies and institutions, such as regional biodiversity strategies, must be established for effective conservation outcomes. Moreover, citizens’ awareness of the biocultural values of shrine forests should be enhanced to maintain their biodiversity.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description:
Abstract
Background: People experiencing homelessness (PEH) and people who inject drugs (PWID) face disproportionate burdens of infection and poor clinical outcomes due to social determinants of health (SDOH) barriers such as unstable housing, limited medication access, and poor follow-up care. The study purpose was to evaluate the impact of a multi-model quality improvement (QI) bundle on outcomes of hospitalized PEH/PWID.
Methods: A pilot QI initiative was implemented at an urban academic hospital in Detroit (June 2022–April 2023) targeting hospitalized PEH/PWID requiring ≥2 weeks of antimicrobials. Bundled prospective intervention included specialty consultation, tailored antibiotic education, medication cost inquiry, Meds-to-Beds delivery, enhanced case management coordination, and referrals to community-based organizations addressing SDOH needs. Ninety-day clinical outcomes were described.
Results: 42 patients were included: 26% PEH, 29% PWID. Patients were predominately men (62%), White (57%), and with a median (IQR) age of 43.5 (32.5–53) years. Common infections included bacteremia (60%), bone/joint infections (50%), and endocarditis (31%); Staphylococcus aureus was the leading pathogen. Over half of patients were discharged on oral antibiotics. Design: Retrospective case series.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Evaluation of effectiveness of a regional remote antimicrobial stewardship program
oai_dc:dc.dc:description:
Abstract
Objective: Antimicrobial stewardship programs (ASPs) are designed to optimize antimicrobial use for healthcare facilities and are required at all acute care and critical access hospitals (CAHs). However, rural CAHs often lack the resources to implement robust ASPs. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the impact of adding regional remote antimicrobial stewardship services across a 14-hospital system consisting of one acute care and thirteen CAHs.
Methods: Remote ASP expansion consisted of adding an infectious disease (ID) pharmacist and two ID physicians (0.3 FTE) to provide daily stewardship activities including prospective feedback on antibiotic optimization and use education through remote chart review and communication. Antimicrobial utilization, cost savings, and Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) rates were tracked. Intervention data and acceptance rates were also collected.
Results: In the first twelve months following regional remote stewardship expansion, the ASP demonstrated a $619,053.97 reduction (56% decrease in Antibiotic Cost/CMI adjusted patient days) in antimicrobial expenses. While only aztreonam use was significantly reduced at the acute care facility (P < .01), the use of vancomycin, meropenem, linezolid, and aztreonam decreased by 33%, 31%, 18%, and 35%, respectively, among the CAHs (P < .001). A 53% reduction in CDI rates was observed across the health system (P < .01). The program averaged 92 interventions per month, with an overall intervention acceptance rate of 86%.
Conclusions: Remote ASPs represent a viable strategy for extending antibiotic stewardship expertise to resource-limited settings to achieve financial and clinical benefits.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Reference ranges and influencing factors of pressure pain threshold in Chinese patients with knee osteoarthritis
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Background Pressure pain threshold (PPT) is a reliable objective measure of pain sensitization; however, standardized region-specific reference data for Chinese patients with knee osteoarthritis (KOA) remain scarce. PPT at the medial knee and dorsal forearm was assessed using standardized PPT assessment. Demographic characteristics, body mass index (BMI), sociological factors and Central Sensitization Inventory (CSI) scores were collected. Nonparametric analyses, Spearman correlation and hierarchical regression were performed.Results KOA patients exhibited significantly lower median PPTs (forearm: 3.79; knee: 4.21 kg·cm−2) compared with controls (forearm: 5.53; knee: 6.57 kg·cm−2; all p < 0.001), with left-shifted and broader 95% reference ranges (KOA: forearm 2.16–6.09; knee 2.07–6.78 kg·cm−2). CSI scores were moderately negatively correlated with forearm PPT (r = −0.567) and weakly correlated with knee PPT (r = −0.389; all p < 0.001). After adjusting for confounders, CSI remained the strongest independent predictor of PPT (forearm: β = −0.403; knee: β = −0.301; all p < 0.001), explaining greater incremental variance (ΔR2 = 0.144 for forearm; ΔR2 = 0.080 for knee) than other factors. The strong correlation between CSI (subjective) and forearm PPT (objective) provides a preliminary basis for future preoperative stratification and potential perioperative analgesic strategies, with potential clinical translational value.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description:
Background and purpose: Squamous cell carcinoma of the anal canal (SCCA) is a rare malignancy with limited treatment options for advanced or metastatic disease. Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have shown durable responses in clinical trials, but evidence derives from small and highly selected populations. This study investigates the effectiveness and tolerability of pembrolizumab in an unselected real-world cohort.
Patient/material and methods: This retrospective, multicenter cohort study evaluated the real-world efficacy, durability, and safety of pembrolizumab in Danish patients with advanced or metastatic SCCA treated between September 2018 and September 2023. A total of 37 patients, who received at least one dose of pembrolizumab for non-resectable, recurrent or metastatic disease, were included (89% ≥ 2nd line). Median age was 64 years, the majority were female (64.9%), and most tumours were human papillomavirus (HPV) (p16) positive (73.0%).
Results: The objective response rate (ORR) was 13.5%, with two complete and three partial responses. The clinical benefit rate (CBR) was 48.6%, and two patients had durable responses exceeding 24 months. Median progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were 4.0 months 95% confidence interval (CI) (2.6–5.5) and 12.1 months 95% CI (7.6–15.2), respectively. Patients with good performance status and HPV-positive disease had significantly improved survival outcomes. Treatment was well tolerated, and no treatment-related deaths were reported.
Interpretation: In this real-world cohort, pembrolizumab demonstrated durable responses in a subset of patients with advanced SCCA and an acceptable safety profile. Outcomes were comparable to clinical trial data, indicating modest activity. Findings support using pembrolizumab as a treatment option in selected patients, but further evidence is needed to refine its role.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Efficacy and safety of vismodegib in periocular and orbital basal cell carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: BackgroundPeriocular and orbital basal cell carcinoma (BCC) represents a therapeutic challenge due to its proximity to critical structures, the risk of disfigurement, and the potential need for exenteration in advanced disease. Vismodegib, a Hedgehog pathway inhibitor, offers a non-surgical alternative, but its overall efficacy and tolerability in this subset remain unclear.AimThis systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and recurrence outcomes of vismodegib in periocular and orbital BCC.MethodsA systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted. Eligible studies included prospective or retrospective cohorts and case series with ≥7 patients treated with vismodegib. Primary outcomes were complete and partial response rates; secondary outcomes included recurrence, exenteration, and adverse events. Pooled incidence rates with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated using a random-effects model.ResultsEighteen studies, with 764 patients, were included. The pooled complete response rate was 38.4% (95% CI: 36.6–57.4), and partial response occurred in 39.2% (95% CI: 32.4–47.5). Recurrence following discontinuation was reported in 17.4% (95% CI: 7.0–30.3). Despite vismodegib therapy, exenteration was performed in 28.1% (95% CI: 12.3–34.5). oai_dc:dc.dc:title: From a monotypic genus to a western Balkan radiation: the remarkable diversity of Xerocampylaea (Gastropoda: Hygromiidae)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The Balkan Peninsula is one of the most important biodiversity hotspots in Europe, but the western Balkans, especially Bosnia and Herzegovina, remain understudied. We studied a poorly known and taxonomically challenging clade of land snails that comprises species previously assigned to the genera Xerocampylaea, Trochulus, Monachoides and Semifruticicola. In a first comprehensive assessment of the group since 1915, we investigated its morphological diversity and mitochondrial phylogeny and we attempted to link these two sources of information with available nominal taxa. A total of 70 populations representing most of the clade’s distribution and ecological ranges were analysed. The oldest available name for the clade is Xerocampylaea, which until the first molecular phylogenetic analyses was considered a monotypic genus. In our preliminary taxonomic treatment, we identified 13 mitochondrial lineages that match a more or less diagnosable morphotype with a defined distribution as well as an available name: X. zelebori, X. erjaveci, X. hirci, X. osoria, X. blaui, X. floerickei, X. costulata, X. waldemari, X. leptolasia, X. serbica, X. fallax, X. taraensis and X. kosovoensis. The combination of microsculpture, genital features and geographic location enables their fairly accurate identification. To stabilize the nomenclature and remove ambiguities in type localities and the interpretation of taxa, we designated five lectotypes and three neotypes. However, there still remain lineages that may represent unnamed species and names that cannot be unambiguously linked to a biological species. Our study of the Xerocampylaea group constitutes a great step towards a better understanding of the complex pattern of genetic and morphological diversity in Balkan land snails, but should be followed by even more detailed studies employing genomic data.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Guidelines for Estimating the 3D Size and Shape of Boulders from Planetary Surface Images
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The shape of boulders on planetary surfaces can be used to investigate the geological processes that influence them and to estimate key surface mechanical properties. The resulting 3D size and shape parameters, estimated from 2D images, closely match the true 3D parameters derived from LIDAR data. We conclude with a set of recommendations for performing reliable morphological analyses of boulders and particles in 2D planetary images, including considerations of image resolution and sample size.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Superelastic alloys for critical applications in extreme environments are required to combine a wide operating temperature range, low temperature sensitivity, and high strength.
